kitDescription: D: Killer Wife is a Fire-element Sniper Rifle Supporter on Burst I with a 20s cooldown. Her Skill 1 gives herself a one-shot Pierce tag every 3rd full-charge shot, and on every Full Burst entry she hands a 13.55% Pierce Damage buff (10s) to every Sniper-Rifle ally, herself included. Her Skill 2 is the real support channel: every 8 full charges she shaves 7 seconds off the whole team's Burst cooldowns (accelerating the rotation all fight), and every 5 full charges she gives all allies +5.06% Attack Damage for 10 seconds. Her Burst fires a 269.28%-of-final-ATK hit at the enemy nearest the crosshair and stamps it with Wipe Out for 10 seconds. While Wipe Out is up, allies whose normal attacks land on the target get one of two buffs depending on where they hit: hitting destructible parts grants +16.26% core damage, hitting the body grants ATK equal to 12.19% of her own ATK — both for 10 seconds.

redAssertions: fixture non-vacuity → 'her burst really casts' asserts buffApply{coreDamagePct,16.26} exists (witness the driver deliberately deleted)
S1a → expects a gainPierce effect block (driver leaves the line unmodeled/documented)
S2b → expects trigger.kind 'chargeCounter' and the {3,5,8} counter-set, driver ships 'hitCount' {5,8}
burst B parts branch → expects buffApply{coreDamagePct,16.26} to allies (driver removed the branch as an over-credit)
burst B body branch → expects casterAtkPct value-set size 1, observes 2 (blind filter does not isolate by caster; crown's own casterAtkPct contaminates)

skill1.kitLine: Full Charge x3 / self: Gain Pierce 1 shot
skill1.driverSaid: Not encoded; both prose lines carried verbatim in unmodeled.skill1 plus a caveat naming the exact consequence (a tagged shot would become eligible for the 13.55% Pierce Damage-Up during Full Burst → small own-damage undercount).
skill1.blindSaid: S6 models it as chargeCounter:3 → gainPierce durationSec 1.2 (⚑ its own flag: no durationShots primitive exists, 1.2s is an unmeasured stand-in). S5 asserts a gainPierce block exists, but its OWN inertness assertion (teammates byte-identical without the tag) passes against the driver.
skill1.formulaCheck: game-mechanics §11: Pierce core+body double-hit is a MULTI-PART-boss mechanic; PIERCE_CORE_DOUBLE=false on the partless scope-lock boss. So the tag adds no targets and no doubling; its only live channel is the Pierce term in the DamageUp bucket, which needs a live pierce tag to bite. Omission = a bounded undercount, never an over-credit.
skill1.explanation: Deliberate, verbatim-documented skip with the mechanism, the direction of the error, and the blocking primitive named. The blind's own encoding is a flagged ⚑ guess at a duration the schema cannot express ('for 1 shot' has no durationShots on gainPierce), so modeling it would ship an unmeasured number where the driver ships a documented zero. Not a silent drop.

skill1.kitLine: FB enter: SR allies Pierce Dmg ▲13.55%
skill1.blindSaid: S6 identical (alliesOfWeapon SR, 13.55, 10s). S5 GREEN on all four of its S1b assertions, including the weapon-scoping discrimination against liter/crown and the FB-entry-vs-burstCast trigger identity.
skill1.formulaCheck: Prose says 'Affects all allies with a Sniper Rifle' with no except-self clause; she is SR, so self-inclusion is correct. Pierce Damage ▲ is a DamageUp-bucket entry (damage-calculation §1e, gated on pierce-tagged hits) — the buff APPLIES unconditionally on FB entry and only converts to damage for a pierce-tagged holder, which is exactly what the driver pins (buffApply event, not damage).
skill1.explanation: Trigger, target scope, value, duration and bucket all match prose + SSOT. Driver test W2 pins distinctFrames === fbFrames (once per FB entry, 6/6) and discriminates against the pre-2026-07-20 all-allies encoding, which reaches the MG ally.

skill2.kitLine: Full Charge x8 / allies: Burst CD ▼7s
skill2.driverSaid: hitCount count:8 → allies → burstCdr seconds:7, recurring (no oncePerBattle). Documented as the 2026-07-16 parser-bug fix (was shotFired → fired every shot).
skill2.blindSaid: S6 chargeCounter:8 → allies → burstCdr 7 (same magnitude, same recurrence). S5 RED on the primitive NAME only; every behavioral assertion (CDR accelerates the rotation; the 8-threshold is load-bearing vs 5) is GREEN.
skill2.formulaCheck: game-mechanics §7 / damage-calculation §2a: auto play ALWAYS releases at full charge (DATAMINED, einkk NikkeFullChargeMode.always). For a 1-hit-per-shot SR, hitCount and a full-charge counter are the same sequence; the ~2% early-release rate is an explicitly unmodeled global, not a per-unit encoding error.
skill2.explanation: Behaviorally identical to the prose counter over the 180s fight (~floor(105/8) ≈ 13 firings, respecting the 6-round magazine + 141f reload dead-time). The blind writer's own spec concedes 'SR always full-charges in-sim so hitCount≈chargeCounter'. RECON_ERROR-class over-specification of the primitive name, not a faithfulness divergence; a chargeCounter re-key would be a zero-behavior-delta readability cleanup.

skill2.kitLine: Full Charge x5 / allies: Atk dmg ▲5.06% 10s
skill2.driverSaid: hitCount count:5 → allies → buff attackDamagePct 5.06, durationSec 10; separate block/counter from the 8-count CDR.
skill2.blindSaid: S6 identical stat and value (attackDamagePct, not atkPct) on chargeCounter:5. S5 GREEN on bucket, ally target set, 10s finiteness and counter separation; RED only on the primitive name.
skill2.formulaCheck: 'Attack damage ▲' is the DamageUp bucket (damage-calculation §1e), NOT the ATK-stat bucket §1a — the two dilute differently against the rest of the comp's supports. Driver uses attackDamagePct; the nearest-wrong atkPct encoding is absent from the event log.
skill2.explanation: Driver test W4 pins distinct firing frames === floor(shots/5) = 21, three targets per firing, 600f window, and discriminates against the hitCount-1 parser-bug class. Counter is independent of the 8-count block (separate block, separate buff key).

burst.kitLine: Deals 269.28% of final ATK addl dmg
burst.driverSaid: burstCast → enemy → flatDamage atkPct 269.28 (lv10), no explicit noFb (engine forces the burst-cast exemption).
burst.blindSaid: S6 identical magnitude with an explicit noFb:true, flagged as convention-not-measurement. S5 GREEN (real damage for her, inert for teammates, correct value).
burst.formulaCheck: damage-calculation §1b Full Burst timing rule: damage dealt BY a burst skill at its cast lands before the FB window opens — the engine forces noFb for burst-cast direct damage, so an explicit noFb would be redundant, not additive. Value 269.28 is the lv10 row of description_value_01; no core wording in the prose → core correctly absent.
burst.explanation: 13 casts → 13 nukes, bucket 'burst', fbMajorApplied false on every one (driver test W5), discriminated against the lv1 magnitude 159.12. Blind's explicit noFb and the driver's implicit engine exemption are the same behavior.

burst.kitLine: Inflicts Wipe Out on target 10 sec
burst.driverSaid: targetStatus{name:'Wipe Out', durationSec:10} on the enemy-targeted burstCast block, ordered BEFORE the gated rider block so the same-frame gate reads it.
burst.blindSaid: S6 identical (name 'wipeOut', 10s, same block); S5 GREEN on enemy scoping, 10s duration, name-key match and the both-ways gate non-vacuity (removing the status kills the riders and moves every teammate's total).
burst.formulaCheck: Status is damage-inert by construction — it emits no damageTakenPct and no buff of its own; it exists solely to open the rider gate. Name-keying (self-consistent 'Wipe Out' vs blind's 'wipeOut') is arbitrary as long as inflictor and gate agree, which the driver test asserts.
burst.explanation: Correct 10s window keyed to HER cast (not to FB start, not FB-duration-keyed). Block ordering is load-bearing and is documented as such in the override note.

burst.driverSaid: REMOVED (2026-07-17). Recorded in unmodeled.burst + two caveats with tier (out-of-domain / v1-partless), estimate (small own-comp core bucket) and recipe (requiresTargetStatus 'Wipe Out' + a parts-hit trigger once destructible parts are modeled).
burst.blindSaid: S6 models it as requiresCore + requiresTargetStatus — but its OWN caveat says 'a strict reading would leave the parts branch fully inert … This dual model can OVER-CREDIT when core exposure is high' and its recipe says to drop it to unmodeled absent per-hitter targeting. S5 asserts the buff exists (2 reds).
burst.formulaCheck: The scope-lock boss is PARTLESS (memory/validation basis + game-mechanics §5). No ally can hit a destructible part, so the buff can never be EARNED. Proxying parts:=core makes it apply whenever Wipe Out is live and lifts EVERY ally's Core term in the Major bucket (§1b) at coreExposure 1.0 — a pure invented gain. Driver test W6's counterfactual measures exactly that: re-adding it lifts all three units' totals.
burst.explanation: Removal is the FAITHFUL choice and the repo convention for v1-partless-inert lines (cf. brid's Wind-Code debuffs); it is the blind writer's own strict reading. S5 RED #1 and #5 both hang on a witness the driver correctly deleted — the burst still provably casts via the 269.28 nuke and the body-branch casterAtkPct. Not a gotcha.

burst.kitLine: hit body: ATK ▲12.19% of user's ATK
burst.driverSaid: burstCast → allies → buff casterAtkPct 12.19, durationSec 10, gated requiresTargetStatus 'Wipe Out' AND requiresCore:true — the caveat calls requiresCore a 'core-only proxy until destructible parts exist'.
burst.blindSaid: S6 encodes the BODY branch with requiresTargetStatus ONLY (no requiresCore) and puts requiresCore on the PARTS branch, where the parts→core proxy belongs. Independent, prose-only, and it inverts the driver's gate placement.
burst.formulaCheck: Prose splits the rider by area: 'Allies that hit PARTS' → coreDamagePct; 'Allies that hit the BODY' → casterAtkPct. On the partless boss the only area split the engine models is core vs non-core, i.e. body = NON-core. Gating the BODY branch on requiresCore therefore asserts the opposite of the kit line. Stat/value/target/duration are otherwise correct: casterAtkPct resolves flat as (12.19/100)×caster.staticAtk per damage-calculation §1a ('% of caster's ATK' = caster BASE ATK, added flat outside the recipient's (1+ATK%)), which the driver pins exactly.
burst.explanation: The gate is a leftover of the 2026-07-17 parts-branch removal: requiresCore was the parts→core proxy (the schema comment ties requiresCore to the parts-hit branch), and when that block was deleted the gate stayed on the surviving body block. Board-inert at the scope-lock basis (coreHitRate 1 → gate passes, 13 casts × 3 allies as the driver measured), so no number moves today; but it is semantically inverted, and driver test W7's third assertion PINS the inversion as intended behavior ('at coreHitRate 0 the block is gated out'), when a faithful body branch should be MAXIMALLY live at coreHitRate 0 — every hit is then a body hit.

gotchas.summary: The body-hit rider carries requiresCore:true — the parts-branch proxy gate left behind after the parts branch was deleted — inverting the kit's body(=non-core) condition; the unit test then pins the inversion as intended.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Allies that hit the body: ATK ▲ 12.19% of the skill user's ATK for 10 sec' (the SEPARATE line 'Allies that hit parts' is the core-damage one). game-mechanics §5/§9 + the validation basis: the scope-lock boss is partless, so the only modelable area split is core vs non-core; body = non-core, hence requiresCore is the complement of the stated condition. Blind S6, prose-only and independent, places requiresCore on the PARTS branch and leaves the body branch gated on the Wipe Out status alone — corroborating the prose read. Driver test W7 asserts 0 applications at coreHitRate 0, i.e. it certifies the inverted direction as load-bearing.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Delete "requiresCore": true from the burst body-branch block, keeping requiresTargetStatus 'Wipe Out' as the sole gate (that IS the faithful encoding on a partless boss: every ally normal hit that is not a core hit is a body hit, so the buff is live for the whole 10s window). Zero expected board movement at the scope-lock basis — verify by re-running the graded comps and confirming byte-identical totals, since coreHitRate is 1 everywhere. Then rewrite W7's third assertion to pin the correct direction (buff still applies at coreHitRate 0) and re-point the requiresCore proxy note onto the still-parked parts branch, where it will belong once destructible parts are modeled. Do NOT substitute a tuned value — this is a gate deletion, not a magnitude change.

verdictRationale: Seven of eight kit lines are clean: five FAITHFUL (SR-scoped FB-enter Pierce 13.55/10s; recurring 7s team burstCdr on the 8-count; attackDamagePct 5.06/10s in the DamageUp bucket to all allies; the 269.28 lv10 burst-cast nuke, correctly FB-exempt by the cast-timing rule; the 10s Wipe Out targetStatus with load-bearing block order) and two DOCUMENTED_GAPs that carry estimate + recipe + tier (S1a's one-shot Pierce tag, verbatim in unmodeled with the undercount direction named and the missing durationShots primitive identified; the parts branch, removed 2026-07-17 because a parts:=core proxy on a partless boss is a pure invented lift of every ally's Core term — a removal the blind override's own caveat independently argues for). All six S5 reds are non-gotchas and I rule them so individually: #1 and #5 assert a witness the driver correctly deleted (the burst provably casts via the nuke and the body-branch casterAtkPct); #2 is a documented inert-line omission whose own inertness assertion passes; #3/#4 are primitive-NAME over-specification (auto always full-charges, so hitCount and chargeCounter are the same sequence for a 1-hit SR, and every behavioral assertion is green); #6 is a blind-fixture leak (the casterAtkPct filter is not caster-isolated, so crown's own value contaminates the set). The single REAL-GOTCHA came from cross-checking the blind OVERRIDE, not the blind tests: the body-hit rider carries requiresCore:true, the parts→core proxy gate stranded on the surviving block when the parts branch was deleted, which asserts the exact complement of 'Allies that hit the body' on a boss where body = non-core; the blind writer, prose-only, put that gate on the parts branch instead. It is board-inert at coreHitRate 1 and therefore costs nothing to fix, but I am withholding GO because the driver's own W7 test elevates the inversion from a stale artifact to a pinned, asserted behavior — landing it teaches the wrong semantics to every future reader and to any non-scope-lock basis. GO on a one-token deletion plus a re-pointed test assertion, with a byte-identical-totals check to confirm zero board movement. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: every agent here is Claude, so the convergence on the three full-charge counters (3/5/8) and on flat-resolving casterAtkPct proves stability, not truth — and the cadence tuple (chargeFrames 60, reloadFrames 141, ammo 6) that sets the CDR and Attack-Damage uptimes is datamined and unverified against footage, so all downstream uptimes remain estimates.
